learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how big corporations raise millions by dividing their business into tiny pieces (shares) and selling them to the public!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If a company needs $1,000,000, instead of borrowing from one bank, it divides the amount into 100,000 'shares' of $10 each. Anyone who buys a share becomes a part-owner of the company.
Companies usually don't ask for the full $10 at once. They ask for it in steps: Application (booking the share), Allotment (confirming the share), and Calls (asking for the remaining balance).

When a company is super popular, 200,000 people might apply for only 100,000 shares (Oversubscription). Pro-rata means dividing the available shares proportionally, so someone asking for 2 shares gets 1.
If a shareholder pays the Application money but fails to pay the Allotment or Call money, the company can cancel their membership and keep (forfeit) whatever money they already paid!

fun_activity.title: 🍰 The Pizza Business
fun_activity.instructions: You want to open a pizza shop for ₹10,000. You divide the ownership into 1,000 shares of ₹10 each. Ask 5 friends to 'subscribe' to your shares. If one friend pays ₹4 but refuses to pay the remaining ₹6, you 'forfeit' their shares and keep their ₹4!

exam_tips: 📌 When recording Forfeiture, ALWAYS debit the Share Capital A/c with the 'Called-up' amount per share, NOT the face value (unless the whole face value was called).
📌 Securities Premium Reserve can never be used to pay dividends. It can only be used for 5 specific legal purposes (like writing off preliminary expenses or issuing bonus shares).
📌 Pro-rata calculation for Calls-in-Arrears on allotment is a guaranteed 8-mark question. Always calculate how much 'Excess Application Money' was adjusted toward allotment first!
quick_recap: ⭐ Equity shareholders are the real owners and take the maximum risk.
⭐ Calls-in-Arrears is money shareholders failed to pay; Calls-in-Advance is money paid early.
⭐ Profit on reissue of forfeited shares is transferred to the Capital Reserve Account.
